input.quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
input.rationale:
Section 9.9 gives each Party (including RevMed as against Sanofi) the right to audit the other's financial books and records, so the rule is engaged notwithstanding mutuality. The clause fails the fallback on material terms: (i) the frequency cap is left blank ([***] audits per Calendar Year) and is in any event subject to an open-ended \"unless for cause\" exception, so there is no effective once-per-year limit; (ii) the notice floor is left blank ([***] prior notice); and (iii) the cost-shift trigger is left blank ([***] percent underpayment), so RevMed's obligation to bear its own audit costs is unquantified. We therefore fixed the three fallback parameters (once per Calendar Year, 15 days' notice, 10% underpayment) with minimal reciprocal edits. Two preferred elements are already satisfied and were left untouched: the auditor must be an \"independent auditor of international prominence\" (9.9(a)) and must sign a confidentiality agreement with the audited Party (9.9(d)). The remaining preferred-only points (business hours, off-site conduct, express no-systems-access) are noted but not pressed, as the audit is limited to books and records maintained under Section 9.8 and confers no system access. Section 5.8's mutual right to review Development records for regulatory and patent purposes, and Section 6.9 (Sanofi's audit of RevMed), are not usage audits against us and are not flagged.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.72

proposal.summary: Fix audit frequency at once per Calendar Year, 15 days' notice, and a 10% underpayment cost-shift threshold
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We set the audit parameters at our fallback position: one audit per Calendar Year (deleting the open-ended "unless for cause" exception that removes any frequency cap), at least fifteen days' prior notice, and cost-shifting only where the underpayment exceeds ten percent. The limits remain reciprocal.
